item.title: Remembering Gloria Steinem and her trailblazing fight for women's rights
item.description:
Illinois Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton got Gloria Steinem’s endorsement in her bid for U.S. Senate. But that’s not what matters to her about the feminist icon, who died this week at the age of 92. “She inspired me not just because of what she did that was so very public and out front and trailblazing and history-making and all of those things, but in the many small ways that she encouraged women like me behind the scenes,” said Stratton, who won the Democratic nomination for an Illinois Senate seat . “She was someone who strongly, first of all, believed in women supporting women, and it didn’t just mean, ‘Well and I’m going to endorse you,’ or ‘I’m going to have an event for you,” though she did those things for me in this run for United States Senate. But it’s the notes. It’s the text message that’s encouraging. It’s the willingness to open her home and gather us together to talk about why…

item.title: Volkswagen to cut further 50,000 jobs as it ends row with union over revival plan
item.description:
Under-pressure carmaker will shed 15% of workforce and halve its product line in sector’s biggest ever restructure The car company Volkswagen has approved controversial plans to shed 100,000 jobs in a battle for survival as it faces fierce competition from Chinese rivals. After the latest round of talks this week, the company announced a further 50,000 job cuts and agreed a staggered end to current production at four German plants: Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and the Audi site in Neckarsulm between 2031 to 2034. There are no specific plans beyond that. Continue reading...

item.title: Philippine vice president is ordered arrested for threats against the president
item.description:
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte arrives before the start of her impeachment hearing at the Philippine Senate in Metro Manila on July 7, 2026. —Noel Celis—Pool/Getty Images A Philippine court on Friday ordered the arrest of Vice President Sara Duterte over alleged grave threats to her former ally, President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. , his wife, and a former House Speaker. The warrant against Duterte, 48, set the bail at 120,000 pesos ($1,900) for each of the three counts against her. “Regardless of the question on jurisdiction, she has no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies,” Duterte’s lawyer said in a statement . Duterte has been charged with threatening the lives of Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and his cousin, former House Speaker Martin Romualdez. The case stems from a November 2024 virtual press conference…

item.title: ‘Things happen’: How Vance’s comment on Iran wedding strike fits US pattern
item.description:
US Central Command has released footage that purportedly shows missile and drone strikes being fired at Iranian military targets. Footage of some of the aftermath of the US attacks was shared on social media, showing shrapnel damage on a home in Sirik, southern Iran, where a wedding celebration was taking place. Since publication of this video, Iranian state media has revised the death toll to four people. Iran retaliated shortly afterwards, with video shared by Iranian media said to show missiles being fired towards Jordan. A US Central Command spokesperson said the US was aware of reports of civilian casualties, but that the 'US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps]' Iran accuses US of ‘war crime’ after missile blast kills five people at wedding Continue reading...

item.title: Iranian town mourns after deadly strike on wedding
item.description:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) is conducting an internal review of a civilian casualty incident at a wedding during the strikes in Iran last Tuesday, U.S. officials say. Why it matters: While it still hasn't been confirmed that the incident was caused by the U.S. strike , it is one of the more significant civilian casualty incidents since the war began six months ago. The most significant civilian casualty incident happened on the first day of the war when a U.S. strike hit a school, killing 150 people, most of them children. The U.S. military investigation into that incident is expected to be finalized soon, according to a U.S. official. Driving the news: According to the Iranian Red Crescent, a humanitarian network, five people were killed and 67 wounded in the blast that hit the home where the wedding was happening. item.title: Meloni celebrates milestone as Italy's longest-lasting government
item.description:
Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is celebrating a milestone: her hard-right government is now the longest-lasting in the country's post war history. In a country known for its political instability, it's a notable record. But considerable challenges remain for Italy's first female prime minister, ahead of elections next year. FRANCE 24's Italy correspondent Seema Gupta reports.
